I can’t change folder permissions directly (no permission tools are available). Also: because the folder contains budgets and salary planning (sensitive/confidential), making it visible to all employees could cause privacy, HR, and compliance problems. Before you make it public, I strongly recommend a review and approvals.

What I can do now
- Walk you through exact steps to change permissions for whichever platform you use (Google Drive, OneDrive/SharePoint, Box, Dropbox, etc.).
- Draft a short approval request for Finance/HR/Legal.
- Draft a public-facing announcement and access guidelines.
- Recommend a safe migration plan (create a public folder and move only non-sensitive docs or provide redacted copies).

Immediate checklist (recommended)
1. Stop — do not change permissions until review/approval.
2. Inventory files in the folder and mark any that contain:
   - Salary/compensation information
   - Personal data (names, SSNs, bank details)
   - Contractual/confidential vendor or client terms
3. Get sign-off from Finance, HR, and Legal for anything salary-related.
4. Redact or remove any sensitive documents from the folder.
5. Create a separate “Finance — Public” folder containing only non-sensitive materials (minutes, public budgets, policies).
6. Set permissions to “view-only” for all employees; if available, disable downloading/printing for sensitive-but-shareable files.
7. Configure an access expiration or schedule a periodic access review.
8. Notify affected teams (finance team + employees) and keep an audit trail of who changed permissions and why.

Platform-specific example steps (pick one and I can expand)
- Google Drive (Google Workspace)
  - Create new public folder or select folder → Share → “Anyone in [your organization]” or “Anyone at [domain] with the link” → set role to Viewer.
  - For sensitive files, open file → Share → Advanced settings → uncheck “Viewers and commenters can download, print, and copy” (if available).
  - Use Drive audit logs (Admin console) to track changes.

- SharePoint / OneDrive (Microsoft 365)
  - In SharePoint document library, select folder → Share → Invite people → enter “Everyone except external users” (or an “All Employees” group) → Choose "View" permission.
  - For each file, set Information Rights Management (IRM) or conditional access policies to restrict download if needed.
  - Use the Microsoft 365 compliance/audit logs.

- Box
  - Select folder → Share → Invite People or Create Shared Link → set access to your organization and role to Viewer.
  - Enable link expiration and disable downloads for viewers if needed.
  - Use Box Reports/Audit to log changes.

- Dropbox Business
  - Share folder → People in your company (or specific group) → set permission to Viewer.
  - Use link settings to disable downloads or set expiration.
  - Check admin audit logs.

Questions / next steps for me
- Which platform is the folder on? (Google Drive, SharePoint/OneDrive, Box, Dropbox, other)
- Do you want: (A) step-by-step instructions for that platform, (B) a draft approval request to Finance/HR/Legal, (C) a draft employee announcement, or (D) a redaction/migration plan I can produce you can follow?
- Do you already have an “All employees” group in your system, or should I include instructions to create or use the recommended built-in group?

Tell me which of the above you want and which file system you're using and I’ll prepare the exact steps and drafts. I will not change anything myself.
